title: Driven-job elapsed counter never ticks: '0s elapsed' for a minutes-long export
body:
## Summary
`elapsed(j)` (lib/jobs.tsx:688-689) is a pure string computed at render, and none of its three call sites has a clock, so a driven job's elapsed count freezes at whatever second the last unrelated re-render happened to land on - and when it does show a long run it reads raw seconds ('347s').

## Description
Every job kind is driven now (lib/jobs.tsx:140-156): nothing updates a running job's record until `settle`, so a JobsProvider state change never arrives mid-run. The three surfaces that print the count:
- components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:335 - the bell's running card. Re-renders on tray open, then frozen while open.
- app/_phases/cut/music-video/MusicVideoExport.tsx:37-43 - 'rendering frame-by-frame, then muxing... {elapsed(job)} elapsed'. The hook (useMusicVideoExport.ts:101-118) sets status 'preparing' then 'exporting' after reading asset bytes, then awaits ONE fetch for minutes - so the line reads '1s elapsed' (or '2s') for the entire export.
- app/_phases/frames/music-video/MusicVideoFrames.tsx:29-33 - poster generation, ~57s measured, same freeze.
The docstrings are the spec the code misses: MusicVideoExport.tsx:32 'Real elapsed time, not a fraction'; app/globals.css:347-349 'the elapsed-seconds count beside the sweep carries the same information without moving' - under prefers-reduced-motion the sweep is switched off (globals.css:373) and this frozen number is the ONLY progress signal left, and it says the run started a second ago.
Format: `Math.round(ms/1000)+'s'` gives '347s' where the repo's own duration convention is m:ss (app/_projects/parts.tsx:63 fmtDur, app/_studio/assetParts.tsx:17).

## Flow
- Cut step (music-video) -> Export 1080p -> line shows '1s elapsed' -> 4 minutes pass -> still '1s elapsed' -> reduced-motion user has no other signal that anything is alive.
- Bell open during a recalibrate -> running card shows the second the tray opened, never advances.

## Expected impact
The one surface that answers 'is it still going?' for minutes-long paid work stops lying. Reduced-motion users get the liveness signal globals.css promises them.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - watching an export/poster/recalibrate run, the elapsed count should advance; today it is frozen at render time
Before: 3 of 3 elapsed() call sites render with no clock (NotificationBell.tsx:335, MusicVideoExport.tsx:40, MusicVideoFrames.tsx:31); value advances 0 times during a single awaited fetch; 347 s renders as '347s'
After: 3 of 3 sites read a ticking `useElapsed(job)` (1 s cadence while running and document visible, via lib/usePolling.ts); 347 s renders as '5:47'
Method: simulation - walked every setState reachable during useMusicVideoExport's awaited fetch (none after setStatus('exporting')) and every JobsProvider state change between start and settle (none for a driven job)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/jobs.tsx:688-689 `export const elapsed = (j: Job) => `${Math.round(((j.endedAt ?? Date.now()) - j.startedAt) / 1000)}s``; grep -rn 'elapsed(' app components -> NotificationBell.tsx:335, MusicVideoExport.tsx:40, MusicVideoFrames.tsx:31; grep setInterval/usePolling in those three files + app/_phases/cut/music-video + app/_phases/frames/music-video = 0 hits; globals.css:347-349 reduced-motion claim; MusicVideoExport.tsx:32 docstring.
verify: Add `export function formatElapsed(ms: number): string` (m:ss at >=60 s, 'Ns' below) and `useElapsed(job)` to lib/jobs.tsx (ticks via usePolling(…, 1000, job.status === 'running')). Probe tests/golden-path/job-elapsed.probe.spec.ts: formatElapsed(347000) === '5:47' (red on HEAD: function absent), and a source ratchet over the three consumer files (stripComments) asserting zero `elapsed(` calls remain and each imports useElapsed. CAUTION for the builder: MusicVideoExport.tsx:39 and MusicVideoFrames.tsx:30 wrap the count in role="status" - a once-a-second tick inside a live region is voiced every second; mark the number aria-hidden or move it outside the status element so only the phase text is live.

title: Bell names one job two ways: 'poster-generate running' vs 'Poster generation…'
body:
## Summary
The bell's running and interrupted cards print the raw `JobKind` id, while the event card for the SAME job prints the curated noun from lib/jobs.tsx's JOB_NOUN - so a run is introduced as 'FOLLOWUP RUNNING' and concludes as 'Follow-up returned'.

## Description
lib/jobs.tsx:166-172 declares JOB_NOUN exhaustively over JobKind precisely so a new kind cannot be mislabelled (its docstring, :161-165). It is module-private and used only for event titles (:555). components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:332 renders `{j.kind} running` and :385 `{j.kind} interrupted`, both uppercased by CSS. 4 of 5 kinds differ visibly between the two cards: followup/Follow-up, recalibrate/Recalibration, poster-generate/Poster generation, video-export/Export (research is the only one that matches). The hyphenated machine ids 'POSTER-GENERATE' and 'VIDEO-EXPORT' are the kind of string the user never typed and never sees anywhere else.

## Flow
- Frames (music-video) -> generate poster -> open bell -> 'POSTER-GENERATE RUNNING' -> run settles -> 'POSTER GENERATION RETURNED'.

## Expected impact
One concept, one name across the three bell cards; the exhaustive table that already exists becomes the single source.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a running/interrupted job should carry the same name its result notification will
Before: 4 of 5 JobKinds render under two different names in the bell (2 raw-id sites: NotificationBell.tsx:332, :385)
After: 0 of 5: both sites read `jobNoun(j.kind)` exported from lib/jobs.tsx
Method: probe - source ratchet over NotificationBell.tsx (stripComments) for `{j.kind}` as rendered text; table diff of JobKind ids vs JOB_NOUN values
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/jobs.tsx:166-172 (const JOB_NOUN, not exported), :555 sole use; components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:332 `{j.kind} running`, :385 `{j.kind} interrupted`; JobKind union lib/jobs.tsx:59.
verify: Export `jobNoun(kind: JobKind): string` (reading JOB_NOUN) from lib/jobs.tsx; NotificationBell.tsx:332/:385 render `{jobNoun(j.kind)} running|interrupted`. Probe tests/golden-path/job-noun.probe.spec.ts: (1) stripComments(NotificationBell.tsx) has 0 matches of /\{j\.kind\}\s*(running|interrupted)/ (red on HEAD: 2), (2) jobNoun('poster-generate') === 'Poster generation'. Keep data-testid `bell-running-${j.kind}` untouched - it is a test contract, not copy.

title: Announcer's ONE-WRITER rule has no gate: 67 scattered live-region attributes
body:
## Summary
lib/announcer.tsx:23-26 states rule 2 - 'Components ask this service to announce; they do not scatter their own aria-live nodes' - because two regions updated in the same breath race and the loser is dropped silently. Nothing measures it, and the tree carries ~67 live-region attributes outside the announcer against 5 useAnnounce consumers.

## Description
Raw grep (app, components, lib; *.tsx; excluding lib/announcer.tsx): aria-live= 16 lines, role="status" 23, role="alert" 29 - 67 attribute lines across 45 files. Recent examples of the race shape the rule names: app/playground/shared/shell.tsx:53 FlashLine is a page-level aria-live=polite toast mounted beside the root announcer; MusicVideoExport.tsx:39 and MusicVideoFrames.tsx:30 are role=status progress lines that update at the same instant the bell announces the job's settle through the announcer. Whether every one should migrate is a judgement per site (an inline role=alert error that mounts with its text is a different case from a toast), so this item does NOT migrate anything: it pins today's number so the rule stops eroding while that judgement is made, the same posture check:narration takes for title= (pipeline/check-narration.mjs TITLE_BUDGET). Not a re-proposal of the open 2026-09-06 Notice role=status item - that is one site; this is the count.

## Flow
- A builder adds a new toast with aria-live=polite -> nothing fails -> a second writer races the announcer -> one of two messages is never voiced.

## Expected impact
The rule the announcer's header calls load-bearing becomes a ratchet that can only fall; the next scattered region fails `npm test` instead of landing silently.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every new transient live region should go through useAnnounce; today a new scattered region costs nothing
Before: live-region attributes outside lib/announcer.tsx: 67 lines / 45 files by raw grep; gate count: none
After: same 67 (pinned, post-stripComments figure recorded in the probe); a 68th fails npm test
Method: probe - tests/golden-path/live-region-budget.probe.spec.ts walks app/ components/ lib/ *.tsx, stripComments, counts /aria-live=|role="(status|alert)"/ excluding lib/announcer.tsx
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: grep -rnE 'aria-live=|role="(status|alert)"' --include=*.tsx app components lib | grep -v ^lib/announcer.tsx | wc -l -> 67 (45 files); grep -rln useAnnounce -> 5 consumers; lib/announcer.tsx:23-26 rule 2; app/playground/shared/shell.tsx:53 FlashLine aria-live.
verify: Write tests/golden-path/live-region-budget.probe.spec.ts modelled on object-url-ownership.probe.spec.ts: recursively read app/, components/, lib/ *.tsx (skip node_modules, dot-dirs, lib/announcer.tsx), stripComments from tests/golden-path/_helpers.ts, count matches of /aria-live=|role="(?:status|alert)"/g, expect(count).toBeLessThanOrEqual(LIVE_REGION_BUDGET) with LIVE_REGION_BUDGET set to the measured post-strip count and a header comment citing lib/announcer.tsx rule 2 and 'lower it when you migrate one'. Prove it bites: temporarily add one aria-live to a scratch copy in the test's own fixture (or assert count === budget on HEAD so a +1 is red). npm test green.

lens_checked.visual-craft: lib/jobs.tsx, lib/announcer.tsx, lib/GlobalErrorBridge.tsx render no chrome of their own (announcer regions are sr-only at :239-256; the other two return Provider/null); their rendered output is strings - checked JOB_NOUN (:166), interrupted error (:267), 'Stopped by you.' (:407) against NotificationBell.tsx consumers
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: elapsed() (:688) traced to all 3 call sites and their re-render triggers; start() refusal path (:599-604) returns null - callers checked at useMusicVideoExport.ts:101-102 (silent return, guarded by UI busy state)
lens_checked.state-coverage: usePolling.ts hidden/visible branches; jobs readStore interrupted path (:264-268) vs bell interrupted card copy (NotificationBell.tsx:421) - Job.error for interrupted is never rendered (grep of .error among useJobs consumers: 0), so its 'The prototype cannot reattach' wording is inert, not a finding
lens_checked.copy-auditor: JOB_NOUN vs bell raw kinds; claudeCli.ts CliError messages (:100-325) and api/recalibrate + api/frames detail strings - real errors, exempt; GlobalErrorBridge route to reportTaskTrouble (bell copy TROUBLE_WORD['non-storage'] belongs to ui-shell)
